questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: It was mostly because I wanted to get out of my comfort zone and to move some boundaries

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted it to be inside of Europe so that I automatically got the Erasmus grant and so that if anything went wrong, it was easier for me to get home

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU did pretty good but my host university didn't give me a lot of information until 1-2 days before I was supposed to be at the welcome session

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, I had to text the international office a couple of times to get help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: In general, it's quite hard to find accommodation in Barcelona and it's way more expensive than you would think. It's crucial to start looking quite early and to ask around if people may know something or someone. For Barcelona, a lot of people use Badi

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing much, it's like living on your own in Copenhagen or any other city but it's nice to have roommates, especially in the beginning and they might be able to help you with a variety of stuff

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Something that weren't mentioned when you applied for the University of Barcelona was that very few courses are taught in English and if you had Spanish in school, you will be not be prioritized for the English courses and you might have to take them in either Catalan or Spanish. 
They give you a folder via mail with a lot of information about the university and the different courses that are taught in English and you're lucky if the description of the course is available in English

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had to text the international office at my host university a couple of times to get help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and stay calm, they are not in a rush in Barcelona which is very frustrating when you come from a country like Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses in itself were okay but the exams were not well planned and therefore I had 4/5 in one week with three of them in two days which made it incredibly difficult to have time to study for all of them in such a small amount of time

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses only had lectures and lab sessions and therefore we didn't have questions or classes where we had the chance to use the material that we just learned, we just had to memorize everything. We also didn't have books and so all the information that they taught us was only based on what they said in the lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Virology
Cytology
Immunology
Cancer Biology
Transgenesis and Animal Improvement

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cancer Biology is interesting but the teacher is quite harsh and the course is quite difficult
Transgenesis and Animal Improvement is also quite interesting because you actually had to think rather than just memorize everything and we use transgenesis and a bunch of research so it was pretty informative to have this course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, the university itself had courses in different sports that you could do and Erasmus Barcelona had a lot of activity that you could participate in

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sagrada Familia with ESN and the Rupit tour with ESN were really good and it made Sagrada Familia affordable for students
Doing a hike on Montserrat and Tibidabo

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Doing a hike on Montserrat and Tibidabo
Visiting Valencia and Madrid
The first Sunday in the month, a lot of the museums are free
Go to the Hospital de Sant Pau

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the people are very friendly and way more outgoing than Danish people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to the Erasmus events, here you can socialize with the local Erasmus coordinators
Take courses the courses in Catalan and Spanish

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that the Spanish system is incredibly inefficient and the sense of time is very different

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Eating out is really affordable and the people are very nice

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient, everything will work out and remember to have fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The T-jove card is the best one to get for transportation, try to look it up before going to Barcelona

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of cool people and really challenging yourself

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having the time to do everything that you want because suddenly the 5 months are up and you have to go home:(

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
